newsitem.title: GERMANY: Greenpeace holds soy protest at Nestle Deutschland.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace holds soy protest at Nestle Deutschland.

text.p: Environmental group Greenpeace on Tuesday staged a protest outside the German headquarters of Nestle Deutschland AG, part of the Swiss Nestle SA group, over the use of genetically modified soybeans in foodstuffs.
"Nestle can't and won't guarantee consumers that its products are free from genetically altered soybeans," campaigner Dieke Bobbink said by telephone from outside Nestle.

"This is part of a multi-country protest calling on food producers to boycott genetically altered soya products and to support the separation of modified and traditional soybeans at origin," she added.
A Greenpeace statement issued in Hamburg said the organisation was demonstrating in Spain, Italy, France, Belgium, Switzerland and the Czech republic.
Apart from Nestle, it had targeted Anglo-Dutch food group Unilever and France's Danone.
Opposition in Europe has focused on the newly imported herbicide resistant RoundUp Ready soybeans, which have been cleared for processing into soyoil and meal by Brussels.
Developed by U.S. chemicals firm Monsanto Co, the beans account for a small part of the U.S. soybean crop this year but they are mixed in with conventional beans.
Bobbink said the Greenpeace protest action was meant to sent out a strong signal that consumers wanted the new beans handled separately, especially if farmers were planning to grow more this year.
"It's also meant to signal to Brazilian farmers (who plan to plant Roundup Ready soybeans in the next crop) that European consumers are opposed to the beans," she said.
Greenpeace cites unknown health and environmental risks.
Nestle Deutschland had been targeted because its headquarters said the group would use soyoil derived from genetically altered beans even though its German subsidiary had said it would not.
Bobbink said consumers had no way of checking if Nestle confectionery on offer in Germany was imported.
